name: path_marquee_encloses
_comment: PATH-element marquee and lasso, five vectors. Until they landed, hit_test had 44 vectors and not one carried a path-command list, so the S-4 relational pass (a leading ClosePath contributes nothing) had nothing to probe here -- and hit_test's element arms are a path CONSUMER. The two `_at_origin` vectors are the discriminating ones: they sit on (0,0), where a mishandled leading ClosePath leaves a spurious subpath start, so they catch the failure mode where the walk EMITS something extra rather than the one where it returns nothing. All five are hand-derived: the path spans x in [3,13], y in [2,9].

name: line_translate_marquee_crosses
_comment:
TRANSFORM + ANTI-VACUITY FLOOR for the element-level families (element_intersects_rect / element_intersects_polygon), declared 2026-07-30. READ THIS BEFORE DELETING OR WEAKENING ANY VECTOR BELOW.

WHAT THE TWO FUNCTIONS MEAN, which is what every `expected` below is derived from: an element is HIT when the selection region meets the element's PAINTED geometry in DOCUMENT space -- for a filled element the closed painted area, for an unfilled (stroke-only) element the outline curve alone -- where document space is the element's local geometry mapped FORWARD through common.transform. Stroke WIDTH is not part of the test (geometric outline only); every vector here keeps a margin far larger than its stroke so the question never arises.

WHY THE BLOCK EXISTS. Before it, all 15 element-level vectors carried transform:null, so the inverse-map branch of element_intersects_rect -- which since 2bb65ca6 is the ONLY path a transformed element takes, marquee AND lasso -- was entered by not one corpus vector in any port. The per-port unit tests that do exercise it use only Line and Rect, the two kinds with real arms in element_intersects_polygon_local, so nothing anywhere could see a kind that reaches that function and yields nothing.

THE FLOOR. For every element kind this corpus can construct WITHOUT a document resolver -- line, rect, ellipse, polyline, polygon, path, text, text_path, group, layer, live/compound_shape -- the corpus must carry at least:
  (a) one HIT and one MISS on the rect-marquee path under a NON-IDENTITY transform;
  (b) one HIT and one MISS on the lasso-polygon path under a NON-IDENTITY transform;
  (c) an IDENTITY-vs-NULL CONTROL PAIR -- the same element, the same region, one with transform {a:1,b:0,c:0,d:1,e:0,f:0} and one with transform null. An identity matrix moves no point, so the two are the same drawing and their expected values are equal BY CONSTRUCTION. A port that answers them differently is deciding on whether the field is present, not on geometry;
  (d) for every kind that can be drawn stroke-only, a MISS whose region lies strictly INSIDE the outline and touches no ink. This is the vector that forbids a bounding-box shortcut, and it is also the one a vacuous arm passes for the wrong reason -- so it never counts as coverage on its own;
  (e) a MARQUEE/LASSO EQUALITY TWIN: for at least one hit and one miss per kind, the same point set expressed once as a rect and once as its 4-point outline. The two entry points must agree about one region.
A kind whose vectors all answer the same constant is VACUOUS and does not count as covered: an arm that can only ever say false satisfies every MISS in the corpus.

DECLARED EXCLUSIONS, with their reasons -- these are NOT claimed as covered:
  * live/reference, live/recorded, live/generated need an ElementResolver (a document, or the concept registry) that a standalone element fixture has no way to supply. Parsed alone their geometry is legitimately empty, so the only honest vectors here are the three resolver-less MISSes at the end of this block. Their real coverage -- a symbol instance is unhittable by marquee AND lasso in both active ports, transform or no transform, because segments_of_element returns [] for them and both catch-alls are segments-based -- belongs in a document-context corpus and is a NAMED OPEN GAP, not a silence.
  * `circle` exists only in the reference (jas/geometry/element.py); neither active port's Element carries the kind, so it cannot be expressed in a shared corpus at all.
  * A SINGULAR transform whose collapsed image still meets the region (scale(1,0) flattening a stroked shape onto a line that crosses the marquee, say) is deliberately NOT pinned here: whether a zero-area image paints is a ruling, not arithmetic. The one singular vector below keeps its region clear of the collapsed image so it needs no ruling.
why: translate(100,50) maps the segment (0,0)-(20,0) to (100,50)-(120,50). The marquee is [110,120]x[45,55]; the sub-segment from (110,50) to (120,50) lies in it (50 is in [45,55]) -> the painted curve meets the region -> HIT.

name: line_translate_marquee_elsewhere
why: Same doc segment y=50, x in [100,120]. The marquee is [110,120]x[60,70]; y=50 is not in [60,70] and the segment has no other y -> disjoint -> MISS.

name: line_translate_lasso_crosses
why: EQUALITY TWIN of line_translate_marquee_crosses: the same point set [110,120]x[45,55] written as a 4-point outline. Same region, same drawing -> same answer, HIT.

name: line_translate_lasso_elsewhere
why: EQUALITY TWIN of line_translate_marquee_elsewhere -> MISS.

name: line_rotate90_lasso_crosses
why: rotate90 = {a:0,b:1,c:-1,d:0} maps (x,y) to (-y,x): (0,0)->(0,0) and (20,0)->(0,20), so the doc segment is x=0, y in [0,20]. The lasso is the box [-5,5]x[5,15]; the sub-segment x=0, y in [5,15] lies inside it -> HIT.

name: line_rotate90_lasso_elsewhere
why: Same doc segment x=0, y in [0,20]. The lasso is [5,15]x[5,15]; x=0 is not in [5,15] -> MISS.

name: line_identity_marquee_crosses
why: CONTROL PAIR (identity leg). Identity moves no point, so the doc segment is the local one, (0,0)-(20,0). The marquee [10,14]x[-5,5] contains the sub-segment from (10,0) to (14,0) -> HIT. Must equal line_null_marquee_crosses.

name: line_null_marquee_crosses
why: CONTROL PAIR (null leg). Same element with transform:null and the same marquee [10,14]x[-5,5] over the same segment (0,0)-(20,0) -> HIT. Equal to the identity leg by construction: an identity matrix and no matrix describe the same drawing.

name: rect_filled_scale2_marquee_inside_fill

name: rect_unfilled_rotate90_marquee_inside_outline
why: STROKE-ONLY INSIDE-MISS. rotate90 maps (x,y)->(-y,x), so the corners (0,0),(20,0),(20,10),(0,10) go to (0,0),(0,20),(-10,20),(-10,0): the doc outline is the boundary of [-10,0]x[0,20]. The marquee [-6,-4]x[8,10] sits strictly inside it -- 4 units clear of the x=-10 and x=0 edges, 8 and 10 clear of the y edges -- and an unfilled rect paints only its outline, so the region touches no ink -> MISS.

name: rect_unfilled_rotate90_marquee_crosses_outline

name: rect_filled_identity_marquee_inside_fill

name: rect_filled_null_marquee_inside_fill

name: ellipse_filled_scale2_marquee_encloses
why: scale(2) maps the ellipse to centre (20,20) with semi-axes 12 and 8, so the doc shape occupies [8,32]x[12,28]. The marquee [0,40]x[0,40] contains that whole box, hence the whole painted disc, which is non-empty -> HIT. The headline case: a marquee that ENCLOSES the drawn shape.

name: ellipse_filled_scale2_lasso_encloses
why: EQUALITY TWIN of ellipse_filled_scale2_marquee_encloses -> HIT.

name: ellipse_unfilled_scale2_marquee_crosses_outline
why: Doc outline: centre (20,20), semi-axes 12 and 8. Its rightmost point is (20+12,20) = (32,20) and the marquee is [28,36]x[16,24], which contains it (28<=32<=36, 16<=20<=24). Genuinely a CROSSING, not a containment: (28,20) is inside the outline (((28-20)/12)^2 = 0.444 < 1) while (36,20) is outside (((36-20)/12)^2 = 1.78 > 1) -> HIT.

name: ellipse_unfilled_scale2_lasso_crosses_outline
why: EQUALITY TWIN of ellipse_unfilled_scale2_marquee_crosses_outline -> HIT.

name: ellipse_unfilled_scale2_marquee_elsewhere
why: Doc shape spans [8,32]x[12,28]; marquee [100,110]x[100,110]. 100 > 32 -> disjoint -> MISS.

name: ellipse_unfilled_scale2_lasso_elsewhere
why: EQUALITY TWIN of ellipse_unfilled_scale2_marquee_elsewhere -> MISS.

name: ellipse_unfilled_scale2_marquee_inside_outline
why: STROKE-ONLY INSIDE-MISS. Doc outline: centre (20,20), semi-axes 12 and 8. Every corner of the marquee [18,22]x[18,22] is strictly inside it -- the farthest, (22,22), evaluates ((22-20)/12)^2 + ((22-20)/8)^2 = 0.0278 + 0.0625 = 0.0903 < 1 -- and the region is convex, so it never reaches the curve. An unfilled ellipse paints only that curve -> MISS. This is the vector that forbids a bounding-box repair.

name: ellipse_filled_scale2_marquee_inside_fill
why: Same region as ellipse_unfilled_scale2_marquee_inside_outline but FILLED, so the interior is painted and [18,22]x[18,22] (worst form value 0.0903 < 1) lies wholly within it -> HIT. The pair isolates fill from geometry: identical region, opposite answers.

name: ellipse_filled_scale2_marquee_bbox_corner_outside_fill
why: INVERSION PROBE. Doc ellipse: centre (20,20), semi-axes 12 and 8; its bounding box corner is (8,12). The marquee [8,10]x[12,14] sits in that corner, INSIDE the bbox but OUTSIDE the ellipse: the form ((x-20)/12)^2 + ((y-20)/8)^2 is convex with its minimum at the centre, so over the box it is minimised at the nearest corner (10,14), giving (10/12)^2 + (6/8)^2 = 0.6944 + 0.5625 = 1.2569 > 1. No point of the region is painted -> MISS. A bbox-shaped answer says HIT here, which is why this vector is in the floor.

name: ellipse_filled_scale2_lasso_bbox_corner_outside_fill
why: EQUALITY TWIN of ellipse_filled_scale2_marquee_bbox_corner_outside_fill -> MISS.

name: ellipse_filled_translate_marquee_encloses
why: translate(100,50) maps the ellipse to centre (110,60), semi-axes 6 and 4, occupying [104,116]x[56,64]. The marquee [100,120]x[50,70] contains that box entirely -> HIT.

name: ellipse_unfilled_translate_lasso_crosses_outline
why: Doc outline: centre (110,60), semi-axes 6 and 4; its topmost point is (110,60-4) = (110,56), which lies in the lasso box [106,114]x[52,58]. A true crossing: (110,52) is outside (((52-60)/4)^2 = 4 > 1) and (110,58) is inside (((58-60)/4)^2 = 0.25 < 1) -> HIT.

name: ellipse_unfilled_translate_marquee_inside_outline
why: STROKE-ONLY INSIDE-MISS under translate. Doc outline: centre (110,60), semi-axes 6 and 4. The marquee is [108,112]x[58,62]; its four corners all sit at offset (+-2,+-2) from the centre, giving (2/6)^2 + (2/4)^2 = 0.1111 + 0.25 = 0.3611 < 1 -- well inside -- so the convex region never meets the curve -> MISS.

name: ellipse_filled_rotate90_marquee_encloses
why: rotate90 maps (x,y) to (-y,x): the centre (10,10) goes to (-10,10), the local x semi-axis 6 becomes the doc y semi-axis and the local y semi-axis 4 becomes the doc x semi-axis. The doc ellipse is therefore centred (-10,10) with semi-axes 4 in x and 6 in y, occupying [-14,-6]x[4,16]. The marquee [-20,0]x[0,20] contains that box -> HIT.

name: ellipse_filled_rotate90_marquee_elsewhere
why: Same doc ellipse, spanning x in [-14,-6]. The marquee [0,4]x[0,4] starts at x=0 > -6 -> disjoint -> MISS.

name: ellipse_unfilled_rotate90_lasso_crosses_outline
why: Doc outline centred (-10,10), semi-axes 4 in x and 6 in y; its leftmost point is (-14,10), inside the lasso box [-16,-12]x[8,12]. A true crossing: (-12,10) is inside (((-12+10)/4)^2 = 0.25 < 1), (-16,10) is outside (((-16+10)/4)^2 = 2.25 > 1) -> HIT.

name: ellipse_filled_lasso_encloses_transform_null
why: NO TRANSFORM AT ALL. The ellipse occupies [4,16]x[6,14] and the lasso is the box [0,20]x[0,20], which contains it -> HIT. element_intersects_polygon is the free-form selection entry point and reaches the same arm with transform:null, so this vector shows the hole is not a transform-only hole.

name: ellipse_unfilled_lasso_crosses_outline_transform_null
why: No transform. The outline's rightmost point is (16,10), inside the lasso box [14,18]x[8,12]. Crossing: (14,10) is inside (((14-10)/6)^2 = 0.444 < 1), (18,10) is outside (((18-10)/6)^2 = 1.78 > 1) -> HIT.

name: ellipse_unfilled_marquee_crosses_outline_transform_null
why: EQUALITY TWIN of ellipse_unfilled_lasso_crosses_outline_transform_null: the identical point set [14,18]x[8,12] written as a marquee rect. Same region, same drawing -> same answer, HIT. The two entry points may not disagree about one region.

name: ellipse_unfilled_lasso_inside_outline_transform_null
why: STROKE-ONLY INSIDE-MISS with no transform. The lasso box [9,11]x[9,11] has its farthest corners at offset (+-1,+-1) from the centre: (1/6)^2 + (1/4)^2 = 0.0278 + 0.0625 = 0.0903 < 1, so it is strictly inside and touches no ink -> MISS.

name: ellipse_filled_marquee_encloses_transform_identity
why: CONTROL PAIR (identity leg). An identity matrix moves no point, so the doc shape is exactly the local one: centre (10,10), semi-axes 6 and 4, occupying [4,16]x[6,14]. The marquee [0,20]x[0,20] contains it -> HIT. Must equal ellipse_filled_marquee_encloses_transform_null.

name: ellipse_filled_marquee_encloses_transform_null
why: CONTROL PAIR (null leg). Byte-identical element and marquee to the identity leg but with transform:null. Same drawing, same region -> HIT. Answering these two differently is deciding on whether the field is present, not on geometry.

name: ellipse_filled_marquee_bbox_corner_outside_fill_transform_identity
why: CONTROL PAIR, other direction (identity leg). Local ellipse centre (10,10), semi-axes 6 and 4; the marquee [4,5]x[6,7] sits in the bbox corner. The form is minimised over that box at its nearest corner (5,7): ((5-10)/6)^2 + ((7-10)/4)^2 = 0.6944 + 0.5625 = 1.2569 > 1, so no point of the region is painted -> MISS. Must equal the null leg.

name: ellipse_filled_marquee_bbox_corner_outside_fill_transform_null
why: CONTROL PAIR, other direction (null leg). Same element, same marquee [4,5]x[6,7], same 1.2569 > 1 -> MISS.

name: ellipse_filled_singular_transform_marquee_elsewhere
why: The zero matrix {a:0,b:0,c:0,d:0,e:0,f:0} maps the entire plane to the single point (0,0), so the drawing has zero area and zero length wherever it lands. The marquee [10,30]x[10,30] does not even contain that collapse point (0 < 10) -> MISS on any reading. Deliberately kept clear of the collapsed image so the vector needs no ruling about whether a zero-measure image paints.

name: polyline_filled_translate_marquee_inside_fill
why: translate(200,0) maps the implicitly-closed square [0,100]x[0,100] to [200,300]x[0,100]. The marquee [240,260]x[20,40] lies wholly inside that painted area -> HIT.

name: polyline_filled_translate_marquee_elsewhere
why: Doc fill spans [200,300]x[0,100]; marquee [400,410]x[400,410] -> disjoint -> MISS.

name: polyline_filled_translate_lasso_inside_fill

name: polyline_filled_translate_lasso_elsewhere
why: EQUALITY TWIN of polyline_filled_translate_marquee_elsewhere -> MISS.

name: polyline_unfilled_rotate90_marquee_on_missing_close
why: OPEN-RUN DISCRIMINATOR. rotate90 maps (x,y)->(-y,x), so the four points become (0,0), (-100,0), (-100,100), (0,100) and the UNFILLED run paints three segments: y=0 from x=-100 to 0, x=-100 from y=0 to 100, and y=100 from x=-100 to 0. The closing edge from (0,100) back to (0,0) -- the doc line x=0 -- is NOT painted, because a polyline's implicit close belongs to its fill, not its stroke. The marquee [-2,2]x[40,60] straddles exactly that unpainted line and is 40 units from y=0, 40 from y=100 and 98 from x=-100 -> MISS.

name: polyline_unfilled_rotate90_marquee_crosses_run
why: Same doc run. The marquee [-52,-48]x[-2,2] straddles the painted segment y=0, x in [-100,0] (0 is in [-2,2]; [-52,-48] is inside [-100,0]) -> HIT.

name: polyline_unfilled_rotate90_lasso_on_missing_close
why: EQUALITY TWIN of polyline_unfilled_rotate90_marquee_on_missing_close -> MISS.

name: polyline_unfilled_rotate90_lasso_crosses_run
why: EQUALITY TWIN of polyline_unfilled_rotate90_marquee_crosses_run -> HIT.

name: polyline_filled_identity_marquee_inside_fill
why: CONTROL PAIR (identity leg). Doc fill = local fill, the closed square [0,100]^2; the marquee [40,60]x[20,40] lies inside it -> HIT.

name: polyline_filled_null_marquee_inside_fill
why: CONTROL PAIR (null leg). Same square, same marquee -> HIT.

name: polygon_filled_scale2_marquee_inside_fill

The marquee [10,14]x[10,14] is 10 units clear of the x=0 and y=0 edges and 26 clear of the x=40 and y=40 edges, so it touches no ink -> MISS. Identical region to polygon_filled_scale2_marquee_inside_fill, opposite answer: the difference is the fill.

name: polygon_unfilled_scale2_lasso_inside_outline

name: polygon_unfilled_scale2_lasso_crosses_outline

name: live_reference_unresolvable_translate_marquee_miss
why: DECLARED-EXCLUSION VECTOR, and it pins only what it can. A live/reference resolves its geometry through an ElementResolver -- a document. Parsed standalone, as this corpus must, the target 'no_such_symbol' resolves to nothing, so the instance draws nothing anywhere and any region misses it -> MISS, translate and all. THIS DOES NOT COVER THE KIND: with a RESOLVABLE target both active ports still answer MISS for every marquee and every lasso, transform or not, because segments_of_element returns [] for reference / recorded / generated and both the rect and the polygon catch-alls are segments-based. A symbol instance is unhittable. That is a NAMED OPEN GAP whose home is a document-context corpus.

name: live_recorded_no_inputs_scale2_marquee_miss
